main_text.l: folo ministratorio, quia in ratione Ecclesiæ Do-
minus summum ius imperiumque semper &
constantissimè sibi vindicauit. Itaque in Politi-
co fuit ordo potestatum inter se, cum summæ
quæ regia dicebatur, cum vero inferiorum ex
ordine : quem ordinem potestates illæ omnes,
& inter se ipsæ, & erga eos qui ipsis suberant &
commissi erant administrationi ipsorum, ob-
seruabant. In Ecclesiastico vero erant omnia
ministratoria, à solo Dei imperio pendentia, &
ad vniuersi vtilitatem solùm pertendentia: adeò
vt ne ipsi quidem sacerdoti summo liceret in re
incognita quidquam, nisi consulto ore Domi-
ni, statuere : quemadmodum aliquot exemplis
in libris Mosis oftenditur.
De his ergo potestatibus tria funt quæ Pro-
pheta hoc versu distinctè prædicat: Primum,
quod nam fit officium harum potestatum : Se-
cundum, qui custodes officij : Tertium deni-
que qualis earum constitutio à Domino. Offi-
cium demonstrat Psaltes[?], cum thronos appellat
iuri : custodes & ϱομοφύλακας[?] exprimit, dicen-
do, thronos domui Dauidis institutos : Constitu-
tionem verò pauculis verbis declarauit dicens:

l.i: illic confidere: id autem est, Hierofolymis.

page.notes: Long s rendered as s throughout. Greek words in the printed text are "thronos" in Latin-looking letters as they appear on the scan, and "ϱομοφύλακας" is a doubtful Greek reading; "Psaltes" is doubtful. Tertium, Psaltes and the Greek word are marked [?]. "Hierofolymis" is read as printed. The "K" at the foot is a gathering signature. The side fragments are show-through and are not transcribed.
